aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.description: Our history and the values that guide everything we do.
aboutPage.foundingNote: JCI Phnom Penh was established in 2010 and officially recognized in 2012.
aboutPage.historyBody1: JCI Phnom Penh was founded by a group of young professionals who believed Cambodia's next generation of leaders needed a space to practice leadership before they were handed it — through real community projects, not just theory.
aboutPage.historyBody2: Since then, the chapter has grown into a volunteer-run network running monthly general membership meetings, skills trainings, and community development projects across Phnom Penh and neighboring provinces, in partnership with local government, businesses, and the global JCI network of over 100 countries.
aboutPage.valuesSubtitle: Every JCI chapter in the world builds its projects and trainings around these four pillars.
aboutPage.valueBusinessBody: Skills training, networking, and mentorship for young entrepreneurs and professionals.
aboutPage.valueCommunityBody: Hands-on projects that address local needs — from clean water to disaster relief.
aboutPage.valueInternationalBody: Exchanges, partnerships, and friendships with JCI chapters across the globe.
aboutPage.valueIndividualBody: Leadership training that turns members into confident public speakers, project managers, and changemakers.

aboutCambodiaPage.title: JCI Cambodia
aboutCambodiaPage.description: The national organization connecting every local JCI chapter across the Kingdom.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyLead: JCI Cambodia is a very young organization compared to most other JCI National Organizations around the world and in the Asia Pacific area. However, JCI Cambodia is a very proud and strong National Organization with a great passion to provide positive change to our community.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody2: Back in 2008 and 2009, the aim of creating JCI Cambodia was to unite and utilize local business networks in Phnom Penh. The implementations, however, did not turn out as we, the founding members, had expected. We experienced trials and errors in many projects. Soon later, we learned that JCI is not only a place to create business networks alone. We learned that JCI's strength is with the passion of its like-minded members to learn how to lead and to change to be better.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody3: In 2010, a few founding members managed to contact Mr. Chy Sila, co-founder of CBM Corporation and Sabay Digital, to help set up an officially recognized association in Cambodia. After researching, training, and encouraging JCI around the world, Mr. Chy Sila agreed to join and had the association legally recognized by the Ministry of Interior later in 2010. He formed a committee of young entrepreneurs and young professionals in Phnom Penh to work on many communities and business-related projects. Soon JCI Cambodia was officially approved to be a Potential Member and Provisional Member in 2010 and 2011 respectively. In 2012, the second National President of JCI Cambodia, Mr. Kouch Sokly, and his board of directors led JCI Cambodia to become a FULLY AFFILIATED JCI Member at the World Congress in Taiwan.
aboutCambodiaPage.historyBody4: Starting with less than 10 founding members, today JCI Cambodia has over 200 members and over 100 volunteers run by seven local chapters. We are on our way to creating more chapters in the near future.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody1: More than 30 years ago, there were efforts in creating a JCI National Organization in Cambodia. Due to wars and other political instability, the setup was not successful. In 2007, two outstanding Cambodian students, Mr. Va Vireak and Mrs. Lay Kanika, who were doing a short management and entrepreneurial course at the Cambodia Japan Cooperation Center (CJCC), were invited to attend the Young Leader Summit, organized by JCI Japan. They met with the 2007 JCI World President and other JCI National Presidents from Asia-Pacific.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody2: In 2008, together with Mrs. Lay Chanrasmey, Mr. Chhen Chandara, and Mr. Heng Samnang, they were motivated and encouraged to formulate JCI in Cambodia with a visit from the APDC team, and conducted the Global Training School (GTS). From 2008 to 2009, the Asia Pacific Development Council made several trips to Cambodia to recruit and motivate more key business leaders to join the set up of JCI Cambodia.
aboutCambodiaPage.aboutBody3: In 2010 and 2011, Mr. Chy Sila began forming a committee to get the organization officially recognized by JCI as well as the Cambodian government. In 2012, JCI Cambodia's National President, Mr. Kouch Sokly, and the board of directors succeeded in getting approval from JCI, making JCI Cambodia a FULLY AFFILIATED member of JCI.
aboutCambodiaPage.missionBody: To provide development opportunities that empower young people to create positive change.
aboutCambodiaPage.visionBody: To be the leading global network of young active citizens.
